summary: 100-foot steel lookout in Carter County, MO, completed 1936 for the Forest Service near Eastwood; keepers named 1936-46; no later record found.

staffing.status: half-time tower tender in 1936; U.S. towerman in 1938; last named keeper moved away by March 1946

facts.agency: Mark Twain National Forest (1936 items say the tower was for the forest service)

events.note: CCC crew erected the telephone line for the planned tower, which was to stand near the cemetery (April 11, 1935 item)
Foundation excavation began in May 1936; solid rock slowed the work into June (items of May 21 and June 4, 1936)
Lookout tower for the forest service completed by August 13, 1936; the page's 1936 note gives a 100-foot steel tower
Odis White given a half-time post as tower tender, alternate days with another man; residence being built at the site (September 3, 1936 item)
Joe Donley replaced Youle Iller at the fire tower (December 3, 1936 item)
Otis White listed as U.S. towerman at the Eastwood fire tower (August 4, 1938 item)
Oades White, keeper of the Eastwood tower, moved from Eastwood to Birch Tree; paper presumed he transferred to Shannon County (March 14, 1946 item)

corrections.why: Wikipedia places the community inside the Mark Twain National Forest, and the 1936 items say the tower was for the forest service. The page header says only 'National Forest'. Medium confidence: the community sits in the forest, but the tower's exact boundary status is not stated.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1935 item said the tower would be erected down near the cemetery; 1936 items place it about a mile east of Eastwood on the Bark Camp road. The story uses the 1936 location.
Items spell the keeper's first name Odis (1936), Otis (1938) and Oades (1946). The story reports the spellings as printed and does not assume they are one man.

notes_for_editor: Read the Central US Lookouts page (quoting 1935-1946 local papers) and Wikipedia; two WebSearch queries found no other record of the tower. Fate, present condition and access are not in any source, so they are left out. The 100-foot height in the page matches the brief's 30.5 m, and the Eastwood index record also gives 100 ft, so there is no height conflict to resolve. The agency correction is the only proposed change to the brief. The 1935 cemetery location and the 1936 Bark Camp location disagree, and the story flags it.
